violations.text: The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety that is registered with the RIDOH Center for Food Protection. CFSM License Application supplied to PIC at the time of inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

A bag of onions and a 2 boxes of muffin mix were observed to be adulterated due to rodent droppings/urine. Food items were voluntarily disposed of by the PIC at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

Several items in the food establishment were observed not marked with the date of preparation. PIC was able to confirm time of prep within the past 7 days. Food items prepared and held for longer than 24 hrs. or portioned from bulk are to be marked with the date of preparation Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

The presence of mice is not controlled as evidenced by droppings and urine on floor, shelving, and food items. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests must be controlled by routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests, using acceptable methods to control pests, eliminating harborage conditions, and routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies. Pest control reports were not available for review at time of inspection. PIC is to ensure: - Pest control to perform a pest inspection prior to next food safety inspection - All food items and single use items are protected from contamination by storing in plastic bins/tubs with lids or kept in original packaging - Any trapped/dead mice are removed and noted for pest control purposes - Facility equipment food contact surfaces and canned goods are properly cleaned and sanitized daily prior to start of use - Search for and seal any possible entry points - Keep the bottom shelf of the food storage shelving clear of any product. - Maintain the pest log provided by the pest technician to aid in the pest control program - Maintain any possible door entry points are well sealed (door sweeps) - Follow any suggestions provided by pest control technician to help eliminate the current pest problem New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

The non-food contact surfaces of the storage shelving were observed to have an accumulation of droppings and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces are tio be cleaned as often as necessary to be cleaned and to aid in the pest control program. New Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

The floor in the back shelving area was observed to have an accumulation of droppings and debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean and to aid in the current pest control program. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 05/19/2026

The back storage area floor was observed to have an accumulation of old droppings/debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean and to aid in the current pest control program. Per the PIC, debris/droppings to be cleaned same day. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 09/16/2025

Unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment or items were observed in the dry storage area. Establishments shall be kept free of unnecessary and/or non-functional equipment and litter to prevent harborage conditions and to aid in the current pest control program. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 10/31/2025

The non-food-contact surfaces of the plastic containers used for storage of non-food and non-food contact items were observed to have an accumulation of old droppings. Non-food-contact surfaces are to be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 05/15/2025

The back storage area floor was observed to have an accumulation of old droppings/debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean and to aid in the current pest control program. New Violation. Correct By: 05/15/2025

At the time of inspection, a package of shredded cheese was observed to be adulterated by mold growth. Shredded Cheese was voluntarily disposed of by the PIC at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/15/2024

Sliced Cheese, Shredded Cheese, and Cooked Taco Meat were observed not marked with the date of preparation/thawing. Sliced cheeses and Shredded Cheeses are to be dated with the date of opening, and food prepped on site is to be dated with the date of preparation and held for no longer than 7 days from the date of opening unless frozen. If food item is frozen, the opening of the packaging, or the preparation of the food item is to be counted as day 1, and when the food item is pulled from the freezer for thawing, the item is to be redated/held for use for no longer than 6 days. Cheeses and taco meat were voluntarily disposed of by the PIC at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 10/15/2024

The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety at all times when time temperature control for safety (TCS) food is being prepared, handled, and/or served. New Violation. Correct By: 05/23/2024

Popcorn chicken was observed held at 119 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be maintained at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or above except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. PIC re-heated food at time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/23/2024
